I STILL don't know how to feel about this game. It looks like so much work has gone into what appears to be a stepping stone to a greater game. Is exploration all that's needed for people to enjoy a game? Minecraft relies on exploration but the purpose of that game is to survive and create. NMS's purpose is to reach the centre of the galaxy... but that doesn't really require work, it just requires time.

This game has so many clicks and whistles, and it DOES look great... but I'm a little more cautious now that I've seen numerous other hype trains derail. This game could deflate upon its release.

So what I feel is that a small company worked really hard on the base of a fantastic game. But it's only a base. The game still needs to be made. Does that make sense? Does anyone see NMS differently?
Let's talk about No Man's Sky

I think that the developers are quite smart in that they offer some really impressive features but I think the depth of the features aren't too deep.

What I mean by that is that they will offer a set of well rounded features (trading, combat, crafting, exploration, etc.) but the features themselves will be relatively simple compared to a game similar to, say, EVE Online. This will allow them to actually finish the game(!) and ensure that that the game is fun and balanced.

If you are concerned that the game won't have enough to do, check out this video for information on the trading system.

I'm a little more cautious now that I've seen numerous other hype trains derail.

I feel the same and I hope that No Man's Sky turns out as they advertise it to be. However I don't think it will be a game I'm hooked on as it appears to mainly exploration which I find can become boring, like in games such as Minecraft. I personally prefer objective-based games with clear goals. Saying that, there aren't as many games being as original so I'll probably end up buying it.
